subject: Columbus Elementary School Renaming
overview: The Medford School Committee voted to rename the Christopher Columbus Elementary School to the Missituk School following an advisory committee presentation and extensive public comment. The committee also received COVID-19 health updates, recognized district retirees, updated several administrative policies, and passed resolutions regarding universal free school meals and meeting start times.

items.title: COVID-19 Health Update and Director Retirement Recognition
items.summary: Director of Health Services Toni Wray presented a final summary of the district's COVID-19 surveillance and pooled testing program, after which school leadership and committee members recognized Wray for her service upon her retirement.

items.title: Global Scholars Student Petition on Electric Vehicle Chargers
items.summary: Seventh-grade students presented a climate action project advocating for public electric vehicle charging stations at local schools, leading the committee to approve a motion to assess and install at least one EV charger per school parking lot.

items.title: Columbus Elementary School Renaming Presentation and Vote
items.summary: The advisory committee presented three finalist options—Missituk, Jean Barry Sutherland, and Belinda Sutton—and following extensive public comment, the School Committee voted four-to-three to rename the building the Missituk School.

items.title: Approval of Minutes, Bills, and Financial Matters
items.summary: The committee approved meeting minutes from May 24 and June 7 as amended, as well as routine bills, payrolls, and fund transfers.

items.title: Rules, Policy, and Equity Subcommittee Report
items.summary: The committee approved three policy updates recommended by the subcommittee, incorporating floating lunar and Eid holidays into the school calendar, revising the public participation guidelines, and adopting a new structured agenda format.

items.title: Special Education and Behavioral Health Subcommittee Update
items.summary: The committee accepted an update from the subcommittee regarding trauma-informed school initiatives, mental health training, and inclusive curriculum pilot programs.

items.title: Superintendent's Report, MHS Signage, and Employee Retirements
items.summary: The committee received district updates, approved the student-selected entrance sign option for Medford High School, and accepted the official recognition report for 2021 district retirees.

items.title: FY22 Budget Update and Meeting Schedule
items.summary: Administration presented revisions bridging the discrepancy between committee requests and the mayor's municipal recommendation, and the committee voted to hold its final FY22 budget meeting on June 24, 2021.

items.title: Resolutions on Meeting Schedule, Free Meals, Facilities, and Condolences
items.summary: The committee withdrew a plaque proposal, approved resolutions setting a 6:30 p.m. regular meeting start time and implementing universal free school meals for 2021–22, requested a high school air conditioning cost report, and offered condolences for deceased community members.
